title: Review garden playbook (micro-experiments & follow-ups)
content:
Purpose: rapid scratchpad for tiny review heuristics, safe micro-refactors, and followups I can run between meetings. Not polished — notes to self + quick commands.

High-level goals:
- Keep review time < 30m for small PRs (<= 200 loc).
- Surface regression risk quickly (tests+canary slices).
- Prefer non-invasive fixes first; leave complex rollouts for scheduled windows.

Fast risk checklist (one-line, use in PR description):
- Does this touch hot-path (inference loop, KV cache, batching)? -> escalate
- New dependency? -> require security signoff
- DB/Schema change? -> migration plan + backfill
- Behavior change for clients? -> update compat tests + changelog
- Performance-sensitive loop? -> add microbenchmark snippet

Quick review heuristic (order I skim):
1) Title/desc -> does it explain WHY
2) Files changed -> hotspots flagged (runtime, api handlers)
3) Tests -> unit + integration presence
4) CI -> check flaky tests, timeouts
5) Perf/regression risk -> add perf notes in review
6) Migration/DB -> look for forward/backward compatible steps

Minimal comment templates (copy-paste into GH):
- "Could you add a tiny unit test that exercises the new branch? I want to avoid silent regressions."
- "This is touching hot-path; can you quickly run `bench/infer_small.sh` locally and paste numbers?"
- "Prefer non-invasive: can we do this as a feature flag first?"

Micro-refactor ideas (cheap, low-risk):
- Extract small helper from repeated 8-line block in request parsing -> reduces cognitive load.
- Convert long boolean flag chains to small enum + doc comment.
- Move experimental KV cache toggles behind env var and add a smoke test.

Small experiment plans (1–2 day):
- KV cache TTL tuning (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/487).
  Hypothesis: increasing TTL from 30s to 60s reduces p50 token latency by 5% on synthetic traces with high reuse.
  Metrics: p50/p95 token latency, GPU utilization, cache hit rate.
  Steps: add metric tags, run canary on dedicated pool (10% traffic) for 2h, snapshot traces.

- Batching window shrink experiment
  Hypothesis: small reductions reduce latency tail for low qps endpoints without large throughput loss.
  Quick test: run local harness with qps=5, sequence length distribution A/B.
  Command: `python tools/batch_harness.py --qps 5 --window-ms 8`

Post-merge follow-up template (copy into sprint board):
- Short title: e.g., "postmerge: tighten test for PR#487 (kv ttl)"
- Owner: me or triage oncall
- Why: capture a regression that might appear in staging
- Steps: add integration test, schedule 1h canary, monitor cost/latency for 24h

Notes-to-self: common nit patterns I keep commenting on:
- Hidden side effects in getters (functions that mutate state) -> call out explicitly
- Long parameter lists (>4 args) -> suggest small struct/typed options
- Requiring global state in constructor -> prefer DI via interface

Example quick commands I use during review: 
- Run unit tests for file: `pytest tests/unit/test_x.py -q`
- Run local perf harness: `bash infra/bench/run_local.sh --profile small`
- Trace a request: `curl -H 'X-Debug-Trace: 1' http://localhost:8080/infer`

IRR (interesting refactor runway) list (small things to batch):
- Replace magic numeric constants around cache sizes with named constants + rationale comment.
- Consolidate three identical error messages into a single util to keep i18n consistent.
- Add a tiny benchmark harness to `tools/bench` that can be run by reviewers (single script).

Edge-case checklist I forget too often:
- Behaviour when request.max_tokens == 0 -> reject or pass-through?
- What happens with streaming when client disconnects mid-chunk? Ensure KV cache cleaned.
- Graceful fallback when quantized kernel fails -> should not crash process, record metric and fallback.

Followups for the week (actionable, put into sprint if progress):
- Add `tools/bench/run_local.sh` README + example outputs (owner: Juno)
- Add a tiny CI job: `smoke-light-bench` that runs harness on PRs touching runtime (owner: me)
- Draft doc for "how to review hotpath PRs" (short checklist + sample comments) -> convert to shared drive doc once stable

Random notes / ideas: 
- Could use a lint that flags large diffs touching files under `runtime/hot` and tag them for manual perf review.
- Low-friction canary: route 1% traffic to new revision and auto-fail if p95 increases > 10% for 10m. Is this policy-owned or infra? Tag infra.

Open questions (to resolve in async or chat):
- Who owns the canary routing policy? @Ethan? (asked in #platform-ops)
- Do we have a standard set of microbench configs for PRs? I keep re-creating them. Maybe add `bench/defaults.yaml`.

Scratch: quick diff idea to propose in review for small safety net:
- Add `--safety-check` flag to the runtime binary that runs lightweight validation on model shape + kv cache config at startup. If flag present, fail early with clear error.

Signature: this is my rolling personal checklist — keep short, iterate quickly. Will pull items into formal docs as patterns stabilize.

-- Priya
